item.title: LaMelo Ball lists $2.6 million luxury Charlotte condo after Timberwolves trade
item.description: LaMelo Ball lists $2.6 million luxury Charlotte condo after Timberwolves trade originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LaMelo Ball is officially moving on from Charlotte. The former Hornets star, 25, has listed his luxury uptown Charlotte condo for $2.6 million after being traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves in a blockbuster deal in late June. According to Realtor.com , the 3,495-square-foot property features four bedrooms, four-and-a-half bathrooms, and some seriously luxurious amenities. Located inside The Trust, an exclusive seven-residence building in the heart of uptown Charlotte, the condo offers sweeping city views, soaring ceilings, and marble floors with gold detailing. There's also a gourmet kitchen with a massive waterfall island, a custom wet bar, and an elaborate dressing room that could rival a designer boutique. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Erika Mendoza Charlotte NC (@erika_lmendoza) "Some addresses speak for themselves. Others are reserved for those who value something extraordinary," Coldwell Banker real estate agent Erika Mendoza wrote on Instagram while promoting the luxury listing. RELATED: Devin Booker's Nike Book 2 sneakers get bold graffiti makeover LaMelo Ball's Charlotte condo has surprising connection to NFL star Cam Newton Before becoming an owner, Ball rented the unit from Carolina Panthers star Cam Newton . He later purchased the condo from the NFL quarterback for $2.47 million in 2024, according to the Charlotte Business Journal . He also purchased a second unit in the building on the floor below the property for $2.2 million, per Realtor. Newton isn't the only sports figure with ties to the upscale building. NBA legend and former Hornets minority owner Michael Jordan also owns property there. The listing comes as Ball prepares for his first season with the Timberwolves. The 2021 NBA Rookie of the Year spent six seasons with Charlotte before the June trade sent him and Josh Green to Minnesota in exchange for Naz Reid and future draft picks. item.title: Yankees Provide Injury Update On Aaron Judge
item.description: New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge The New York Yankees played most of the season without Aaron Judge, who missed over 80 games with a rib injury and then suffered a calf strain after returning. Judge's late-season calf injury kept him out of the postseason as well. Now that the season is over, Judge will have time for his calf to heal, but general manager Brian Cashman provided an update on the three-time MVP. "We did exit interviews with everybody, obviously, including Aaron Judge. He was not available to us in the postseason. There was no, you know, there was no willy-nilliness over that. You know, he just wasn't physically able to post for us. So, because of the calf. In terms of the rib, we did the exit interviews, exit physicals, and that all came out fine for us. "And we do have a follow-up with the specialist, (Dr. Gregory Pearl), that has to take place still, just to be certain, because that's the expert in this field. And then once he weighs in, we'll have, you know, that all firmed up one way or the other. But as of right now, we feel like we're in a good place, and, you know, he can take advantage of the rest of the winter and be ready to go when spring training starts." Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! It sounds like the Yankees are expecting Judge to be at 100% by the start of spring training. Manager Aaron Boone also noted that there are no medical procedures currently scheduled for Yankees players. Losing Judge was a huge blow for the Yankees offense, and even when he did return from the rib injury, he injured his calf before he got his timing back. Getting Judge back at full strength will be key for the Yankees next year, but what will be more important is whether he can stay healthy. item.title: LeBron James Spars with Knicks Fans Before Scoring First Win with the 76ers
item.description: LeBron James Credit: Caleb Bowlin/Getty NEED TO KNOW LeBron James interacted with fans at Madison Square Garden The 76ers star was seen exchanging words with at least one fan, according to social media footage At another point in the game, James heard it from the crowd while he was at the free-throw line LeBron James appeared to give a fan an earful in the season-opener against the New York Knicks on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The Philadelphia 76ers star, 41, was seen interacting with at least one member of the crowd at Madison Square Garden during the second quarter. “Ain’t nothing soft in the Midwest,” James appeared to say, according to clips of the tiff . “I don’t know what the f--- you talking about.” He continued, “I’m not from the West Coast. I’m from Ohio. Baby, f--- is you talking about?!” NBC’s Mike Tirico seemed to have intel on the exchange, claiming that fans may have been taunting James over his helicopter commute from his home in New York City to Philly. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! At another point in the game, the former Lakers star got his own earful when he took to the free-throw line. LeBron James heart taunts from the crowd at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday night. Credit: Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty In footage circulating on social media , fans chanted “We don’t want you.” The chirps appear to stem from remarks previously made by the NBA veteran, who contemplated joining the Knicks as a free agent. James signed a two-year, $8 million contract with Philadelphia over the summer after eight years with the Lakers. The NBA’s all-time leading scorer told ESPN last month that he once envisioned wrapping his storied NBA career in New York. James and the 76ers, however, got the last laugh Tuesday, spoiling the home team’s celebratory night — when Knicks players received their rings and unfurled the championship banner — with a 106-100 win. All of which had the NBA legend feeling generous in his comments after his regular-season debut for Philly. “It is a great night for New York fans, 50-plus years. I was a part of that at one point where we hadn’t won a major championship in Cleveland in over 50 years,” James told reporters . “The fans will never forget this moment, and will never forget that championship run. We’re happy just to be able to come and play on such a historical night in a historical building and play the game we love.” Read the original article on People

The Mariners endured a disappointing 2026 campaign, finishing with a losing record and missing the playoffs. Their season included a historic 22-0 defeat to the Milwaukee Brewers on August 18, the worst loss in franchise history. Seattle’s season ended on September 27 following a 7-3 win over the Los Angeles Angels. During the offseason, Arozarena, whose contract expires after the 2026 World Series, was spotted supporting Tampa Bay during its Game 6 victory over the Cleveland Guardians in the ALCS on Monday. His appearance did not sit well with Covino, who called out the Mariners outfielder on a recent episode of “Covino & Rich.” “What are you doing at the game? What are you doing there? You should be embarrassed. You’re a spectator at a game you should be playing in,” Covino said. The radio host also criticized Arozarena’s interaction with Tampa Bay third baseman Junior Caminero after the latter hit a crucial two-run home run. Caminero pointed toward Arozarena in the stands before sharing the outfielder’s signature arms-crossed celebration. Covino questioned the exchange and argued that Arozarena is still an employee. “The home run trot from Caminero. He rounds 3rd, but he stops at home plate right before he steps on home plate, and he looks into the crowd, folds his arms, stands still, looks into the crowd. Now what is he doing? Several key players, including Davante Adams , Romeo Doubs and Terry McLaurin suffered significant injuries in Week 6 that will sideline them for an extended period. At least fantasy football managers know they need to find immediate replacements there. The guys who are questionable, but could play this week are the ones who are most concerning right now. Here are some of the most prominent players dealing with nagging ailments or returning from major issues that will impact fantasy managers most in Week 7. As always, keep an eye on the latest developments leading up to kickoff with our player notes page . WEEK 7 BYES: Buffalo, Jacksonville, L.A. Chargers, Washington WEEK 7 RANKINGS: QB | RB | WR | TE | K | DST | FLEX QB Lamar Jackson, Baltimore Ravens Jackson is still technically day-to-day, although coach Jesse Minter did say on Monday that the former MVP could "potentially" return to practice this week . He has yet to take the practice field since spraining his left ankle in a Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans. If Jackson can't go on Sunday against the Bengals , backup Tyler Huntley will make his third consecutive start. QB Baker Mayfield, Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Bucs are stil preparing for rookie Jalon Daniels to start this Sunday at Carolina. But the ever-insistent Mayfield did take part in Wednesday's practice session while wearing a glove to protect the injured thumb on his passing hand. The big question is whether Mayfield will be able to hold the football securely under game conditions. RB Saquon Barkley, Philadelphia Eagles No news is ... good news? He was scheduled to do some running on Tuesday and then take part in practice the following day. item.description: Luka Doncic reveals where he wants to finish his NBA career originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . If it's up to Luka Doncic, he'll be in Los Angeles for a long time. Ahead of Wednesday's 2026-27 season opener, the six-time All-Star was asked if he wants to retire as a member of the Los Angeles Lakers . His response was encouraging for Lakers fans. “Hopefully, yeah,” Doncic told the California Post's Melissa Rohlin . There was, however, a catch. “But as you know in this NBA business, you never know what’s going to happen. But I feel like I’ve found something here that’s very comfortable for me. And hopefully [that happens].” MORE: Draymond Green boldly predicts Luka Doncic's future with the NBA MVP award Doncic was traded from the Dallas Mavericks to the Lakers in a shocking 2025 NBA trade deadline deal. The 2026-27 season will be his second full season in Los Angeles. The team Doncic joined is very different from the one around him now. Not only is LeBron James no longer on the roster, but the Lakers made a number of offseason additions with Doncic specifically in mind. Whether the Lakers like it or not, Doncic's future in L.A. will become a topic sooner rather than later. He's under contract through the 2028-29 season, although the final season is a $57.4 million player option. That means Doncic would become a free agent after the 2027-28 season if he declines his option. For now, at least, Doncic sounds comfortable in Los Angeles. Whether that leads to him finishing his career in a Lakers uniform remains to be seen. item.title: Royal County Down Submit Plans For Upgrades To Its Championship Course
item.description: NEWCASTLE, NORTHERN IRELAND - SEPTEMBER 10: A general view of the first green as players putt during a practice round prior to the Amgen Irish Open 2024 at Royal County Down Golf Club on September 10, 2024 in Newcastle, Northern Ireland. (Photo by Ross Kinnaird/Getty Images) Getty Images Royal County Down Golf Club, whose championship course is one of the world’s most revered golf courses, stated that they are preparing for work to be done on the Championship course. Royal County Down, which is located in Northern Ireland, consistently ranks as one of the most scenic, and also one of the toughest, golf courses in the world. In fact, has been rated as number one in the World’s 100 greatest and number one in the Best in the United Kingdom and Ireland categories by Golf Digest . It therefore comes as a surprise that Royal County Down Golf Club has announced plans for changes to both their Championship and Annesley courses. In a planning statement submitted by the club , the goal is to “significantly upgrade the course to reflect RCD’s status as one of the very best golf courses in the world and one of the most significant golf tourism assets in Northern Ireland”. Royal County Down has never hosted an Open Championship, and the work could be an attempt to attract an Open Championship in the future. It would make sense then that architecture firm Mackenzie & Ebert was chosen to carry out the work. Mackenzie & Ebert have experience working on Open Championship Rota courses, having done work on eight of the ten venues including Royal Lytham and St Annes, Royal St. George’s, Royal Troon, Royal Liverpool, Royal Birkdale, Carnoustie, Turnberry, and Royal Portrush. Changes proposed by Mackenzie & Ebert include adjustments to existing tee boxes, new teeing grounds, a new green on the 5th hole, as well as reshaping and remodeling of the closing stretch of holes, 16-18. Changes are also proposed for holes 1, 3, 5, 11, and 12. While the planning statement references upgrades to the course to maintain its status quo atop the golf course rankings, it does not specifically state a desire to host an Open Championship. Rather, the statement goes on to say the works will help the club to “continue to attract and support the hosting of large events, building upon the success of the hosting of the Amgen Irish Open in 2024”. While around 70,000 visited Royal County Down during the Amgen Irish Open in 2024, attendance was capped at 16,000 per day. Contrast those numbers with the 2026 Open Championship at Royal Birkdale, which hosted 306,000 fans. While plans have been submitted, they are subject to approval by the planning committee in the district council. If approved, work could begin in 2027. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.description: Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Philadelphia Eagles have faced widespread scrutiny for their handling of quarterback Jalen Hurts’ health over the past two weeks. The franchise announced ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers that Hurts would be out indefinitely due to a superficial blood clot in his calf. Then, news broke on Monday that Hurts would miss the rest of the season after further tests revealed several blood clots in his lungs. The week before, he’d been cleared to play against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London despite having already been diagnosed with blood clots in his calf and advised not to sleep, and also took an international flight home from London with the active blood clots. The Eagles’ handling of Hurts’ health has since been widely questioned, with CBS’ Leger Douzable going as far as to characterize it as “disturbing.” Still, the NFL told The Athletic that the process surrounding the quarterback was “handled appropriately,” and in response to the backlash, NFL Chief Medical Officer Allen Sills spent nearly five minutes on Tuesday defending Philadelphia’s protocol to reporters, asserting that reports insinuating that any of the league’s physicians would put a player in harm’s way are “nonsense.” NFL Chief Medical Officer Allen Sills gave a nearly 5-minute defense of the league and Eagles protocol in treating Jalen Hurts’ blood clots. Called some reports “nonsense” and insisted that no doctors are taking orders from football coaches or management when treating patients. https://t.co/LvmzoYvPYy — Jori Epstein (@JoriEpstein) October 20, 2026 The NFLPA, however, released a statement Tuesday evening stating that the league made it clear it hadn’t investigated the protocol the Eagles followed, and had no intention of doing so before calling for a full investigation: “The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward.” Media members on social media had a wide range of reactions to the NFLPA’s statement and Sills’ address. The NFL wasn’t really telling the truth. item.title: Boban slams Bruno Fernandes: ‘United won’t have a strong future if he’s the best player’
item.description: Boban slams Bruno Fernandes: ‘United won’t have a strong future if he’s the best player’ It’s safe to say that former Milan midfielder and Sky Sport Italia pundit Zvonimir Boban is not a fan of Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes, claiming that the Premier League side ‘will not have a present or future at a strong level as long as he is the best player’. Fernandes was named in the Manchester United starting line-up for their visit to the Stadio Sinigaglia to take on Como in the Champions League league phase on Wednesday evening. You can follow the action from Wednesday’s Champions League matches on the Football Italia Liveblog. Boban critisicm of Bruno Fernandes ahead of Como vs. Manchester United ZAGREB, CROATIA – OCTOBER 25: Former footballer Zvonimir Boban looks on prior to kick off of the UEFA Champions League group E match between Dinamo Zagreb and AC Milan at Stadion Maksimir on October 25, 2022 in Zagreb, Croatia. (Photo by Jurij Kodrun/Getty Images) Boban was among the pundits in the studio for Sky Sport Italia’s coverage of the Como vs. Manchester United match and was asked for his thoughts on United’s captain and star player, Bruno Fernandes. The Portugal international spent five years in Italy at the beginning of his career with stints at Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria, before moving to Sporting CP in 2017. Boban feels that the United captain is a ‘good player’ but feels that they will not be able to compete at the highest levels ‘as long as he is the best player’. LEEDS, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 18: Bruno Fernandes of Manchester United in action during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Leeds United and Manchester United at Elland Road on October 18, 2026 in Leeds, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) “Bruno Fernandes is a good player, but they are acting as if he’s a top star, and he does not belong at that level of football,” Boban told Sky Sport Italia. “As long as he is the best player at Manchester United, then Manchester United will not have a present or future at a strong level. We are talking about a perfectly good player, he understands football, moves in spaces, reads it well, but he is a very long way off the level of what ought to be a leader at a club like Manchester United.”

item.title: Another Star May Have Re-Signed With WWE
item.description: WWE Ivy Nile may have quietly signed a new deal with WWE. According to Fightful Select , Nile’s contract was due to expire at the beginning of October. However, she is still listed as an active talent on WWE’s roster page, and she appeared on the October 6 episode of NXT in a battle royal to determine the number one contender for the NXT Women’s Championship. That match was won by Wren Sinclair, who was impersonating Lady Shani. Her NXT appearance came after a long stretch away from WWE’s main shows. Nile has been off Raw since March, and she has wrestled only two matches on the show this year. Most of her work in 2026 has come on WWE Main Event, where she has wrestled 12 times, including matches against NXT talent such as Thea Hail, Wendy Choo and Lizzy Rain. Fightful Select reported in early September that Nile’s contract was set to expire soon and that it had not heard whether she had negotiated a new deal. The same report said WWE had plans for her and that creative had a “big change” in store. Fightful Select later reported that the change was a tag team with Jordynne Grace. According to Fightful, vignettes pairing the two were filmed over the summer, with the hope that they would air in September, and its sources linked the team to the WWE trademark “Iron Built.” The vignettes never aired. In May 2025, she won the tournament to become number one contender for the WWE Women’s Speed Championship but lost to Sol Ruca in the title match. Grace has also been off television, and a WrestleVotes report said WWE does not have her in its creative plans at the moment, while adding that she is not on her way out. What Ivy Nile’s WWE Contract Status Means Nile still being on the roster is a good sign that the company sees value in her, even after a year in which she was barely used on Raw. Her name staying on the roster page and her appearance on NXT television right after her contract was due to expire both point to her still being under contract, and they suggest the company wants her visible again. The Grace team is still the best path for her. Both women have strength-based styles and are competing in bodybuilding, the vignettes are already filmed, and the women’s tag team division needs new challengers. Tatum Paxley holding the tag titles with Alexa Bliss also gives Nile a built-in story against her former partner. The concern is that WWE has had this plan ready since the summer and still has not pulled the trigger. If Nile did sign a new deal, the company should use it as a reason to finally air those vignettes and give both women something to do on television. item.title: Cowboys are getting dangerously close to thinking about the draft
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There is a point in every disappointing season when the conversation shifts from how a team can make the playoffs to whether it has any realistic chance of competing at all. After another lifeless start and a 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers, the Dallas Cowboys are getting dangerously close to that point. At 2-4, with consecutive losses to Tampa Bay and Green Bay, this team looks less like a playoff contender and more like one that could be picking near the top of the 2027 NFL Draft… if they had that pick. Instead, the New York Jets would likely have it for the Quinnen Williams trade unless the Green Bay Packers fall apart and the one Dallas got in the Micah Parsons trade is even higher up. That is a brutal place to be for a team with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and an offense that entered Week 6 averaging 27.6 points per game. Yet the Cowboys have scored just 29 points combined in their last two games. They were held scoreless in the first half at Lambeau Field for the first time since November 2021, and the offense looked completely out of answers when Green Bay turned up the pressure. Questioning the heart of football players is usually a foolish take. item.title: The staggering distance Kyle Berkshire has just driven the ball to break his own world record
item.description: Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Kyle Berkshire is well known as the longest hitter of the golf ball on the planet. Berkshire won the World Long Drive Championship four times during a five-year period from 2019 to 2023. The 6ft 3in powerhouse generates tremendous speed and has been known to exceed 230 mph ball speeds with the driver. Kyle Berkshire holds numerous records already including the longest drive on a golf course and the longest drive on a runway – 1,060 yards for what it’s worth! Berkshire’s world record long drive on a golf course stood at 579 yards before this week. The 29-year-old set that record in 2023 after clocking a 241.6 mph ball speed with his driver. And now he has beaten that record without reaching a ball speed as high as the one he generated three years ago. The staggering distance Kyle Berkshire just drove the ball to break his own world record Berkshire attempted to beat his world record this week in Rawlins, Wyoming. The long-drive legend posted a video of his attempts to beat his own record to his official YouTube account. The American powerhouse did not let anyone down. He produced an absolute monster of a drive after clocking a 234.2 ball speed. With that swing, he recorded a drive that travelled a total distance of 588.3 yards – an absolutely gargantuan hit. It is worth pointing out that Berkshire’s drive was downhill and downwind, although he only got 48 yards of run. Berkshire carried his ball an incredible 540 yards through the air. If only Kyle Berkshire was able to tone down his speed and was even half decent from 100 yards and in, he would surely be a real force on the PGA Tour. That said, there is plenty of money in online content creation these days, so it might not even be worth his time trying to sharpen up his game in order to compete on professional tours.

item.title: Journo spots Carrick having a ‘robust exchange of views’ with Man Utd starter in first half vs Como
item.description: Journo spots Carrick having a ‘robust exchange of views’ with Man Utd starter in first half vs Como Manchester United have got off to a nightmare start once again in the Champions League by conceding early. Last time out in Europe, Atletico Madrid opened the scoring inside the first minute of action before going on to seal a 2-0 win. Tonight, Como broke the deadlock in just the second minute via a scintillating strike from Nico Paz, making United the first English team in history to concede in the first two minutes of consecutive major European matches, as per Opta. It’s therefore no surprise that, shortly after the opener and United’s torrid start, Samuel Luckhurst spotted Michael Carrick bickering with Matheus Cunha from the touchline. “Carrick just had a relatively robust exchange of views with Cunha during the stoppage before he cursed at MUFC losing possession again,” Luckhurst penned on Twitter/X. Cesc Fabregas’ side have dominated in the first half, and arguably played United off the park for the first half-hour of action. United are now at risk of suffering the same fate they did at the Metropolitano, where they had only very few chances and failed to get back into the game with even one goal. Prior to kick-off, Dimitar Berbatov expressed just how essential it was that his former club left with a win tonight. “If they lose today, the pressure will be even more. They need the win today no matter what. I don’t care how. Long ball, direct ball, possession — just get the win because the pressure will get less after the game,” the ex-striker said on TNT Sports. United’s last win in any competition came on September 10 against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah, while their last Premier League victory was all the way back in August against newly-promoted Ipswich Town. item.title: Rio Ngumoha overtakes Balotelli in Champions League record
item.description: Rio Ngumoha overtakes Balotelli in Champions League record Liverpool forward Rio Ngumoha became the third-youngest player to register two assists in a Champions League match during the Reds' 4-3 win over Villarreal . The 18-year-old provided both assists to move ahead of former Liverpool striker Mario Balotelli , who was 18 years and two months old when he achieved the feat for Inter against Anorthosis in 2008. Only Warren Zaïre-Emery and Theo Walcott were younger when they registered two assists in a Champions League match. Zaïre-Emery was 17 years, seven months and 18 days old when he set up two goals for Paris St-Germain against AC Milan in 2023, while Walcott was 17 years and eight months old when he did so for Arsenal against Hamburg in 2006. Ngumoha had already made history in August 2025, becoming Liverpool's youngest goalscorer at the age of 17 years and one month. If he scores in this season's Champions League, he will also become the club's youngest goalscorer in the competition. That record belongs to Trent Alexander-Arnold , who was 19 years and 11 days old when he scored. Ngumoha has made nine appearances this season and recently made his senior England debut. item.description: Rangers v Middlesbrough - Pre-Season Friendly Rangers FC graphics are outside the stadium during the pre-season friendly match between Glasgow Rangers and Middlesbrough at Ibrox Park in Glasgow, Scotland, on July 26, 2025. Glasgow Strathclyde U… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Ricky Carroll, Editor It might have been Albert Einstein who said something about the definition of madness or insanity being to perform the same action over and over again, but expecting different results, just as Rangers are with Djeidi Gassama. The 23-year-old winger arrived from Sheffield Wednesday in a cut-price £2 million deal last summer, with Owls fans feeling that Danny Rohl had taken advantage of a loophole that saw them robbed of a £10 million transfer windfall. Rangers looked to have pulled a blinder when Gassama hit the ground running in the Europa League qualifiers, only to become the latest in a long line of frustrating wide men. Time for Rangers to Drop Djeidi Gassama IMAGO / Focus Images The Mauritania international has been around professional football for some time and is approaching 200 senior appearances. By now, he should have ironed out the creases that he left Paris Saint-Germain’s academy with as a player with high expectations. His consistency and availability are to be applauded; his end product isn’t. Gassama featured in every league game for Rangers last term and has done so again this term – 47 in total. What frustrates, much like Ryan Kent, isn’t his work rate, attitude, durability, ball carrying, or ability to create space for teammates; it is his goal return. He has one goal in 14 games this season in total, none in the league, to add to his three from last year. Read More: Rangers’ Next £20m Star? Transfer Interest Reported From Top Leagues in Key Man The 10 assists in 70 appearances since he joined is hardly the sort of figure that inspires confidence either. With the same minutes, Scott Wright, Ross McCausland and Rabbi Matondo could all have produced something similar. With Kim Minsu and Badredine Bouanani both proficient dribblers and attacking options, Rangers no longer need to rely on Gassama being the only outlet to progress the play up the park, and it is time for Derek McInnes to give someone else a chance. What Has McInnes Said About Gassama? There is a feeling that every game is going to be the one. But it doesn’t come. Against Dundee, Bouanani did his job on the other flank and was Rangers’ most dangerous player, and yet it was Gassama who played the full 90 minutes. Every shot that Bouanani hit was placed and put on target; only two world-class saves denied him a hat-trick. Despite his fleeting appearances, he looks like the complete package. Gassama though, as McInnes himself admitted recently, via The Rangers Review , needs to start adding numbers: “Particularly in recent weeks he has carried the fight. We’ve built the game well, utilised space and become a very good counter-attacking team, and he’s been a big part of that.

His consistency and availability are to be applauded; his end product isn’t. Gassama featured in every league game for Rangers last term and has done so again this term – 47 in total. What frustrates, much like Ryan Kent, isn’t his work rate, attitude, durability, ball carrying, or ability to create space for teammates; it is his goal return. He has one goal in 14 games this season in total, none in the league, to add to his three from last year. Read More: Rangers’ Next £20m Star? Transfer Interest Reported From Top Leagues in Key Man The 10 assists in 70 appearances since he joined is hardly the sort of figure that inspires confidence either. With the same minutes, Scott Wright, Ross McCausland and Rabbi Matondo could all have produced something similar. With Kim Minsu and Badredine Bouanani both proficient dribblers and attacking options, Rangers no longer need to rely on Gassama being the only outlet to progress the play up the park, and it is time for Derek McInnes to give someone else a chance. What Has McInnes Said About Gassama? There is a feeling that every game is going to be the one. But it doesn’t come. Against Dundee, Bouanani did his job on the other flank and was Rangers’ most dangerous player, and yet it was Gassama who played the full 90 minutes. Every shot that Bouanani hit was placed and put on target; only two world-class saves denied him a hat-trick. Despite his fleeting appearances, he looks like the complete package. Gassama though, as McInnes himself admitted recently, via The Rangers Review , needs to start adding numbers: “Particularly in recent weeks he has carried the fight. We’ve built the game well, utilised space and become a very good counter-attacking team, and he’s been a big part of that. “Gas just needs to improve his numbers. He’s desperate to score more goals, and it’s something he’s aware of. Whether it’s attacking crosses from the opposite side or creating opportunities himself, that’s the one thing he needs to add to his game. “Because the fitness is there, the intent is there, the power is there, and the confidence is there. It’s just that final piece and, if we can put everything together, hopefully he can continue progressing and become a big player for us this season.” Daisuke Yokota being injured has reduced McInnes’ options, although Findlay Curtis and Minsu could both play off the left-hand side of the attack if he wanted to make the change. The Last Word There is no denying that Gassama has everything needed to be a key player for Rangers if they are to win the Scottish Premiership and other domestic trophies this season. He can create something from nothing, and he can score goals when little seems on, but as Light Blues fans saw with Kent, carrying a winger that works hard and plays every game means little when they aren’t scoring goals or creating good chances for their teammates when it comes to silverware at the end of the season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
